summary: Implementation provides proof-of-concept hover type inference. Correctly falls back to primitive/indexed types when inference fails.

correctness.type_environment: build-tenv-from-defs correctly resets type variable counter between definitions
correctness.fallback_strategy: compute-hover correctly falls back to get-type-string when inference fails
correctness.parse_definitions: Correctly extracts both define forms: (define x ...) and (define (f args) ...)

malformed_documents.note: guard clause returns empty list on any parse error - entire document fails silently
malformed_documents.impact: Single syntax error anywhere prevents type inference for whole file
malformed_documents.recommendation: Consider incremental parsing that preserves successfully parsed definitions

circular_references.note: Definitions processed sequentially - forward references not resolved
circular_references.impact: Mutually recursive functions will fail to infer correctly

local_scope.note: Only top-level defines are scraped, not local bindings
local_scope.impact: Hovering over let-bound or function argument variables returns no type

performance.concern: Re-parsing on every hover request - O(N) per hover where N is document size
performance.recommendation: Cache type environment per document, invalidate on change

error_handling.tradeoff: Prevents LSP crashes but makes debugging inference bugs difficult

recommendations: Critical: Make parse-definitions robust to partial syntax errors
Optimization: Cache tenv per Document, invalidate on change
Feature: Multi-pass inference for forward/recursive references
conclusion: The implementation provides basic hover inference that correctly integrates with the existing bidirectional type system. Current limitations (forward references, local scope, re-parsing overhead) are acceptable for initial deployment. The fallback mechanism ensures primitive operations always display types.
